headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a **ready‑made API** that accepts an IP address and returns the associated company (organization) data—including contact information when the provider supplies it. | Service | Endpoint | Key Features | Pricing | Notes | |---------|----------|--------------|---------|-------| | **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | • Organization name & ID
• Contact email & phone (if available)
• ASN, carrier, etc. | Free tier: 50k requests/month. Paid plans start at $5/mo. | Requires API key for higher limits. | | **ipstack.com** | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=` | • Company name & domain
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• ASN, carrier, etc. | Free tier: 10k requests/month. Paid plans start at $10/mo. | Email/phone only in paid tier. | | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | • Organization name
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• ASN, carrier, etc. | Free tier: 30k requests/day. Paid plans start at $9.99/mo. | Email/phone only in paid tier. | | **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=&ip=` | • Organization name
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• ASN, carrier, etc. | Free tier: 1k requests/day. Paid plans start at $19/mo. | Email/phone only in paid tier. | --- ## How to Use ipinfo.io (Example) ### 1. Get an API Key 1. Sign up at . 2. In the dashboard, copy your **API token**. ### 2. Make a Request ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \ https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json ``` ### 3. Sample Response ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` > **Note:** > *The `org` field contains the ASN and organization name.* > *Contact details (email, phone) are only returned in the paid tier.* ### 4. Extract Company & Contact Data ```python import requests API_KEY = "YOUR_TOKEN" IP = "8.8.8.8" headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"} resp = requests.get(f"https://ipinfo.io/{IP}/json", headers=headers) data = resp.json() org = data.get("org") # e.g., "AS15169 Google LLC" # For paid tier: contact_email = data.get("contact_email") contact_phone = data.get("contact_phone") ``` --- ## Choosing the Right Plan | Feature | Free Tier | Paid Tier | |---------|-----------|-----------| | Max requests | 50k/month (ipinfo) | Unlimited (tier‑dependent) | | Contact email | ❌ | ✅ | | Contact phone | ❌ | ✅ | | ASN / Carrier | ✅ | ✅ | | Rate limit | 1 req/s | 5–10 req/s | If you only need the company name, the free tier of any of these services will suffice. If you need contact details, upgrade to the paid tier of the provider that best fits your budget. --- ## Privacy & Compliance - **GDPR / CCPA**: IP addresses are considered personal data in many jurisdictions. Ensure you have a lawful basis for processing (e.g., legitimate interest or user consent). - **Data Retention**: Most providers store data for a limited period (e.g., 30 days). Check the provider’s privacy policy. - **User Consent**: If you’re collecting IPs from end‑users, consider adding a notice or obtaining explicit consent. --- ## Quick Reference – Other Services | Service | Endpoint | Contact Info Availability | |---------|----------|---------------------------| | **ipstack.com** | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=` | Email & phone only in paid tier | | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | Email & phone only in paid tier | | **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=&ip=` | Email & phone only in paid tier | --- ### TL;DR 1. Pick a provider (ipinfo.io is a solid starting point). 2. Sign up, get an API key. 3. Call the endpoint with the IP. 4. Parse the `org` field for company data; upgrade if you need contact details. Happy coding!
